newsitem.title: USA: Datakey sees Q4 charge, no profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Datakey sees Q4 charge, no profit in 1997.

text.p: Datakey Inc, a supplier of electronic products and services, said it expects to record a one-time charge of about $0.08 per share in the fourth quarter. The company also said it does not expect to be profitable in 1997.
It said the charge is related to severance pay and benefits for its former chief executive officer, John Underwood, who on December 3 announced his resignation effective December 31, 1996.
Datakey said sales in the fourth quarter of 1996 and first quarter of 1997 will be lower than in any of the first three quarters of 1996.

"Requested shipment delays from some of our major OEM (original equipment manufacturer) customers have resulted in a much lower revenue expectation in the current quarter and in the first quarter of 1997," said president and chief executive officer Carl Boecher in a statement.
He said OEM customer order backlog is about 30 percent higher than a year ago, but "revenue for 1996 is expected to be about 8-10 percent lower than 1995's $7.2 million revenue."

Boecher said Datakey expects a slight improvement in the quarterly revenue from its OEM business customers as 1997 progresses. In addition, SignaSure EDM, its first end-user product recently released to the market, is expected to contribute incremental revenue in the 1997 first quarter.
But Boecher projected, "Due to a continuing significant investment in product development and promotion, we don't expect to be profitable in 1997."
